# Harness Summary: In-Context Learning Strategy

The harness achieves concerningly low evaluation accuracy across all three datasets (40-48%), with accuracy even dropping below training performance on ds_alpha, indicating overfitting or poor generalization. Every eval failure traced shows the same pattern: the model generates predictions based on "closest demonstrations" in the prompt but consistently misalects against ground truth, suggesting the few-shot retrieval or reasoning strategy fundamentally fails to capture the underlying task logic. Notably, increasing context size dramatically (7.5k to 30k characters in ds_beta) and scaling training examples (84 to 180) yields no meaningful accuracy improvement, pointing to a strategy rather than data/scale issue. The prompting approach appears to rely on loose pattern matching that doesn't work reliably, as evidenced by identical wrong predictions across different problem instances despite varying inputs. Recommend reconsidering the demonstration selection mechanism, prompt structure, or verification logic rather than tuning memory/learning parameters.
